_provenance: GENERATED by book-models/factory_vocabulary_model.py — do not hand-edit; regenerate with `python3 book-models/factory_vocabulary_model.py regenerate`. Derived from the hand-authored vocabulary in book-models/factory_vocabulary_declared.json.
_note: The factory-vocabulary model holds the INTERNAL EDITING vocabulary behind Chapter 5's factory language — never printed in the book. Three kinds of node, not one flat list: a WHOLE (the factory) holding a PART (the fabricator) and a COLLECTIVE (engineering apparatus) whose members are the five KINDs (machinery, tooling, representation, control, infrastructure), plus a PROPERTY (engineering capital) that holds OF accumulated apparatus and an ENVIRONMENT the arrangement creates. Apparatus is the collective noun, NOT a fourth category; capital is a property, NOT a fifth. The kinds OVERLAP by design — `control` names what a decision DOES, not a physical category parallel to tooling — and the `partition` guard carries the closed anti-partition value so no consumer renders them as disjoint bins. `misuse_collocations` and `heterogeneous_list` are the deterministic part a lint can hold (lint_factory_vocabulary.py); the role tests are the part a human applies.

nodes.label: the factory (the production system)
nodes.role_test: Is the referent the WHOLE production system — the arrangement that determines what should be made, organizes how production proceeds, and judges whether what was produced is acceptable?
nodes.negative_rule: Do not use `factory` for one of its constituents. The factory is the whole; the fabricator is a part inside it and the apparatus is the collection of structures arranged around that part.

nodes.label: the fabricator
nodes.role_test: Is the referent the thing that REALIZES the artifact from a description of what should be made?
nodes.negative_rule: Do not call the fabricator `machinery`. It is the PART the apparatus is arranged around — the printer inside the factory — not one of the apparatus's kinds.
exemplars: the printer in the printer metaphor

nodes.label: engineering apparatus
nodes.role_test: Is the referent DELIBERATELY HETEROGENEOUS — several kinds at once, such that naming any single kind would narrow it wrongly?
nodes.negative_rule: Engineering apparatus is NOT a fourth category alongside machinery, tooling, and representations. It is the COLLECTIVE NOUN: machinery, tooling, representations, controls, and infrastructure participate in the apparatus. Do not give it a role test that competes with the kinds' role tests.
exemplars: where the visible engineering apparatus is concentrated
the support apparatus that outgrew the product
the apparatus the weekly series measured

nodes.label: machinery
nodes.role_test: Does it actively PERFORM, ROUTE, COORDINATE, TRANSFORM, or EXECUTE production work?
nodes.negative_rule: Do NOT call a static model, policy, representation, test suite, or human review `machinery` merely because it belongs to the factory.

nodes.label: tooling
nodes.role_test: Is it an INSTRUMENT used to configure, inspect, measure, analyze, or verify?
nodes.negative_rule: `tooling` names what the thing operationally IS; `control` names the constraint it makes consequential. They are different axes, so neither substitutes for the other — a validator is tooling AND, where its verdict gates admission, a control.

nodes.label: representation (model)
nodes.role_test: Does it REPRESENT engineering knowledge or intent in structured form?
nodes.negative_rule: It is not machinery merely because the factory uses it. A representation is consumed BY machinery; that does not make it machinery.

nodes.label: control
nodes.role_test: Does it make an engineering decision CONSEQUENTIAL for later work?
nodes.negative_rule: Do not turn `control` into a physical category parallel to tooling. The categories intentionally OVERLAP: the same validator is tooling by what it is and a control by what its verdict decides. A reading that sorts the kinds into mutually exclusive bins has the model wrong.
exemplars: a ban-lint on a raw seam

nodes.label: infrastructure
nodes.role_test: Is it the COMPUTATIONAL or OPERATIONAL SUBSTRATE that production runs on?
nodes.negative_rule: Do not replace `infrastructure` merely for terminological uniformity. Where the referent is the substrate, the established word is the right one.

nodes.label: engineering capital
nodes.role_test: Does the sentence turn on DURABLE FUTURE LEVERAGE — investment embodied in structures that make earlier engineering work useful to later production?
nodes.negative_rule: Engineering capital is not a fifth category. It is a PROPERTY / INTERPRETATION of accumulated apparatus. Do not repeatedly call everything engineering capital: the empirical claim is that the artifacts ACCUMULATED; capital is the interpretation of what that accumulation is worth to later work.
exemplars: the controls a later Epic inherits without re-deriving them
a validator written once and consulted by every subsequent run

nodes.label: the engineering environment
nodes.role_test: Is the referent what the ARRANGEMENT of apparatus CREATES — the conditions agents produce work inside?
nodes.negative_rule: Do not use `environment` as a synonym for `apparatus`. The apparatus is the collection of structures; the environment is what arranging them produces. One is the inventory, the other the condition.
exemplars: the existing engineering environment shaped how the work could be realized

usage_licences.licence: The support/production ratio measurement — the supporting apparatus weighed against the product it supports. The author calls this "a particularly good use of apparatus".
usage_licences.negative_rule: RETAIN as written. Do not generalize it: outside the support/production measurement, the collective noun is `engineering apparatus`.

usage_licences.licence: An EMPIRICAL / ECONOMIC noun, admitted ONLY where accumulation over time is the measured phenomenon — "the stock of controls" beside a growth curve.
usage_licences.negative_rule: Do not use `stock` as the general conceptual name for factory structures. It is warehouse vocabulary in a factory book; a prior pass drove it from 14 to 0 in the DocAble section, and this narrow licence does not re-open the general use.

misuse_collocations.note: The referent is "tests, static checks, simulators, benchmarks, and policy predicates" — instruments that VERIFY, so `tooling`. Where the sentence turns on the bound being consequential rather than on the instruments, `control` is the other correct reading; the two are different axes, not rivals.

Context is engineering knowledge in structured form: `context representations`, or simply `context`. If the referent is narrowly the retrieval/assembly path that delivers it, that path IS machinery — decide by the role test at the site.
The referent is deliberately heterogeneous ("where the visible engineering apparatus is concentrated"), which is exactly the collective noun's job.
"More of everything" is the collective, not one kind.
What a factory in a box EXPOSES for process design spans kinds — surfaces, representations, and controls — so the collective noun is right.
Making customer intent effective in production IS the control role test: it makes an engineering decision consequential for later work.

NOT a finding. The author defends this phrase twice — in the opening contrast of the two-problems section and again in the factories-inside-and-outside subsection — because DocAble genuinely has orchestration, merge, and execution machinery and the contrast is the argument. Listed so a later pass does not "fix" it.

heterogeneous_list.note: The clearest misuse: a `machinery` TERMINAL closing an enumeration whose members span kinds — "tests, policies, human review, simulators, permission systems, models, or other machinery." A list that spans kinds wants the collective noun, not one of the kinds as a catch-all.
